stories.title: Gut phageome variation is linked to microbial metabolites across a human population
stories.takeaway: A population-level study maps human gut bacteriophages and reports associations with microbial metabolite profiles.
stories.what_happened: Louca and colleagues characterized human gut phage communities and assessed how phage patterns relate to metabolites and microbial ecology.
stories.why_it_matters: Broadens microbiome research beyond bacteria and provides hypotheses for virus–bacterium–metabolite relationships.
stories.caveat: Cross-sectional associations do not demonstrate that phages cause changes in metabolite production.

stories.title: Colonic epithelial cells can regain regenerative potential after radiation injury
stories.takeaway: A study identifies a p53–YSC–YAP signaling axis associated with enterocyte dedifferentiation during colonic regeneration after irradiation.
stories.what_happened: Zhang and colleagues investigated epithelial plasticity and regenerative responses after radiation, identifying a proposed signaling pathway involved in restoring colonic tissue.
stories.why_it_matters: Provides a public experimental framework for studying epithelial repair following radiation-induced intestinal injury.
stories.caveat: Mechanistic findings from experimental systems require validation across human disease settings.

stories.title: Four-dimensional mitochondrial morphology tracks epithelial development
stories.takeaway: Human lung and intestinal epithelial development is accompanied by distinct, potentially predictive mitochondrial-network phenotypes.
stories.what_happened: McMahon and colleagues analyzed mitochondrial-network changes across time and three-dimensional space during human epithelial development.
stories.why_it_matters: Links dynamic organelle architecture to epithelial maturation and offers quantitative phenotypes for tissue-model studies.
stories.caveat: Predictive morphology is not by itself evidence of a causal mitochondrial mechanism.

stories.title: Synthetic gene circuits could enable feedback-controlled cell therapies
stories.takeaway: A review surveys programmable sensor–processor–effector circuits intended to adjust treatment outputs to changing physiology.
stories.what_happened: Ye and Fussenegger synthesize advances in context-responsive and closed-loop gene and cell therapies, including designer cells and engineered microbes.
stories.why_it_matters: Connects synthetic biology, cellular engineering and future adaptive therapies for chronic disease.
stories.caveat: A review of emerging systems is not proof of clinical safety, durable control or effectiveness.

stories.title: Peptide microcondensates enable rapid intracellular delivery of engineered antibodies
stories.takeaway: Engineered IgG–peptide microcondensates delivered antibodies into cells under serum-containing conditions and modulated an intracellular target.
stories.what_happened: Kawaguchi and colleagues engineered anionic antibody tags and membrane-permeabilizing peptide assemblies, visualized uptake, and tested TDP-43 recruitment to stress granules.
stories.why_it_matters: Offers a possible research tool for accessing intracellular targets that conventional antibodies cannot readily reach.
stories.caveat: Cell-based delivery and target modulation do not establish in-vivo efficacy, tissue selectivity or therapeutic safety.
